newsitem.title: RWANDA: OAU peace mission opens talks on Zaire fighting.
newsitem.headline: OAU peace mission opens talks on Zaire fighting.

text.p: An Organisation of African Unity peace mission opened talks with the Rwandan government on Monday aimed at securing a ceasefire in eastern Zaire between Zairean rebels and the country's army.
The rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire have already captured several towns and have vowed to press on with their military campaign to the capital Kinshasa.
The OAU mission, led by assistant Secretary-General Anatole Tiendrebeogo, opened talks with Rwandan Prime Minister Pierre Rwigema, officials said.
The mission will later meet Rwandan President Pasteur Bizimungu and military strongman and vice-president Paul Kagame.
Officials said the OAU mission, which arrived on Sunday from Zaire, is pressing Rwanda to use its influence with the rebels to help secure a ceasefire in eastern Zaire.
